ground_truth.scenario_name: Catalog Service Cache Stampede / Cache Key Corruption
ground_truth.trigger_event: Deployment of catalog-service:v3.1.0 with incompatible Snappy binary cache serializer.
ground_truth.root_cause_summary: Release v3.1.0 introduced an incompatible Redis serialization format (SnappyBinaryCodec) that failed to deserialize existing cache keys. This triggered a total cache hit ratio collapse (98% -> 1.8%) and caused an unmitigated cache stampede onto the primary PostgreSQL database, driving DB CPU to 100%.

expected_evidence_signals.description: Deployment event of catalog-service:v3.1.0 changing cache serializer.
Database CPU reaching 100% under cache stampede.

key_actions: Rollback catalog-service to previous release v3.0.9
Flush corrupted Redis keys with prefix 'catalog:v2' using selective key purge
Implement mutex/singleflight locking on cache misses to prevent raw cache stampedes
expected_remediation.expected_verification_metric: Verify redis/cache_hit_ratio recovers above 95% and database/cpu_utilization drops below 30%.

ground_truth.expected_diagnostic_conclusion: Diagnose catalog-service outage as Cache Stampede / Cache Key Corruption caused by incompatible cache serializer in v3.1.0.

metadata.title: Catalog Service Outage: Cache Key Deserialization & DB Stampede
metadata.impact_summary: Catalog browsing and search completely unresponsive due to database CPU saturation following cache failure.
